license_and_compatibility: No package is added: the shards are GitHub-native parallel steps running the interpreter each production job already uses, and every script of this directory is Python standard library only. Compatibility: each shard is python3 -m unittest -v <test files>, which loads the named modules with the stock loader (load_tests receives the pattern None), so nothing is pickled and dynamically built classes load as they do in production; the inventory gate requires that loading every test file by name gives exactly the ids discovery gives. Shards built from files keep wrapper modules whole. Each job keeps its name, so the required contexts would not change. Module fixtures run once per module as in the serial run, and test files that share a shard share a process; files in different shards no longer share one.

baseline_and_candidate.baseline: Arm S on each runner: python3 -m unittest -v from the checkout root in one step, with the suite environment of the production job (Linux: the four suite-environment steps of validate.yml; macOS: actions/setup-python 3.13 plus the two npm pins, because the trial's jobs are not recorded gaps of the runtime tripwires). That is validate-macos's command and validate's command plus -v for per-test lines.
baseline_and_candidate.candidate: Sharded arms in one parallel group of shard steps, each python3 -m unittest -v <its test files>, the lists built at run time by make_shards.py from the head: on ubuntu-24.04 G4 (4 shards over every test file) and G4T (4 shards without tests.test_secret_path_guard, then that module alone in a serial tail step); on macos-15 G3 and G3T, the same with 3 shards.

predeclared_metrics.quality_rule: Fixed before any hosted run. CORPUS: the whole suite at the draft pull request's head SHA on actual GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 and macos-15 runners, one workflow per OS (suite-shards-trial-linux.yml, suite-shards-trial-macos.yml), each triggered only by the pull request's opened and reopened events with a paths filter on its own file. Every job checks out and asserts the head. INVENTORY GATE: each workflow's inventory job (ubuntu-24.04; the system python3 3.12 for Linux, actions/setup-python 3.13 for macOS) runs inventory.py, which fails the job, so that no arm runs, unless (a) loading every tests/test_*.py by name gives exactly the discovery ids, (b) no id is loaded twice, (c) nothing fails to import, and (d) every test file is in exactly one shard list or the tail of each arm, as built by make_shards.py from the frozen weights; a child interpreter of the gate stopped from outside (SIGKILL, SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP) also fails the job, as an execution problem rather than a finding. ARMS: S, python3 -m unittest -v in one step; G4/G3, one parallel group of 4/3 shard steps, each python3 -m unittest -v <its list>; G4T/G3T, the same without tests.test_secret_path_guard plus a serial tail step that runs that module alone. Each shard step records its exit status and exits with it; its hang guard is timeout-minutes 25 on Linux and 40 on macOS. Three repeats per arm (fail-fast false); Linux at most 2 serial and 2 sharded jobs at once, macOS 1 and 1. The selection metric step_seconds is the test phase from a start step to a stop step (if: always()): the S step, or the group plus the tail, measured with time.monotonic_ns() in two processes, with the wall-clock difference kept beside it. ORACLE: compare.py with its README rules, as frozen here, parsing every log with logparse.py (the first trial's parser, copied unchanged). An S run is eligible when its log has a complete summary and no parse anomaly, its exit status agrees with its status line (zero versus non-zero), its executed ids plus the ids behind a failed or skipped setUpClass or setUpModule are exactly the inventory with each id once, its command is exactly python3 -m unittest -v, git-status.txt (git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all after the run) exists and is empty, run_attempt is 1, checkout_sha is the head, its job was not cancelled, and step_ns and wall_ns are positive and agree within max(5 s, 1 %); the eligible S runs must share one python version. A G or GT run is eligible when every shard log and the tail meet the same log rules, every command is exactly python3 -m unittest -v followed by its list, the run's lists equal the inventory artifact's, each log's executed ids are exactly its modules' ids, the union over all logs is exactly the inventory with each id once (a module in two shards or an id that never started is ineligible), the multiset of (kind, key, outcome) records equals the first eligible S run's outside the flaky ids, every step's probe shows the job's python version and it equals S's, and the checkout, attempt, head, job status and timing rules hold. Flaky ids are ids whose records differ among the eligible S runs; they are listed in result.json and excluded from the comparison. No id is exempt in advance. The inventory artifact must record a passed gate and its lists must equal make_shards.py's lists for its test files and the frozen weights, or the OS gets no verdict. CONTROLS, per OS: one job runs the shard step body in one parallel group on four control modules copied alone into an empty directory, each step with an id (control-0 to control-3) whose own outcome the job's finish step records from the steps context: test_ctl_pass (exit 0, Ran 2, OK at once; step success), test_ctl_hang (a 300 s test under timeout-minutes 1 that appends its monotonic time and parent pid to a heartbeat file every second: stopped, so no exit status and no summary; step failure), test_ctl_fail (one test fails after 90 s: FAILED (failures=1), a non-zero exit; step failure) and test_ctl_crash (os._exit(3) after 120 s: exit 3, no summary; step failure), so the failing and crashing steps must outlive the hang step's stop and each other's failure. The controls pass only when the control job's result is failure, the control artifact holds exactly <os>-controls, every shard behaved as listed with the exact command, each step's own outcome is success, failure, failure, failure (a recorded wrong outcome fails the controls; an unrecorded one is never evidence of failure: when any of the four control steps' outcomes is unrecorded, no recorded one is wrong and every other expectation holds, the controls are unmeasurable, because the steps context carried no outcome for those background steps, and the OS gets no verdict), every background step ran the foreground step's python version and saw SUITE_SHARDS_ENV_PROBE, exported through GITHUB_ENV by an earlier step, the four steps' probes started within 15 s of each other (the hang step is stopped at most 70 s after its start: the 60 s limit, then SIGINT, up to 7.5 s, SIGTERM, up to 2.5 s and a kill, so the failing control outlives that stop and the crashing control outlives the failing control's failure), the hang control's step was stopped at least 50 s after its probe (not before the 60 s limit) and before the failing control's probe plus 90 s (before any sibling could fail, so the limit stopped it), the stop being the first heartbeat with another parent pid (its shell ended while the process lived on) or, when the parent pid never changed, the process's last heartbeat (a process that kept its parent and still beat when the group ended fails), the finish step began less than 240 s after the hang step's probe (the group did not wait for the 300 s test), the control run's checkout is clean, its run_attempt is 1 and its head is the pull request head; a controls-check job (needs controls, if always) asserts this, and the compare job repeats the check on the same artifact: when the controls-check job failed although the repeated check passes, the check job failed outside its checks and the OS is incomplete; when both fail, the controls failed. A control step that left no probe, no log and no exit status although the group started, which only a runner fault does, makes the OS incomplete, its recorded outcome included, unless what the steps that ran recorded shows wrong behaviour (then the controls fail); the start spread and the hang checks then judge only the steps that ran. Reported, not judged: whether background steps start with SIGINT or SIGQUIT ignored (any effect on the suite shows as a record mismatch) and whether the hang control's process outlived its step (its parent pid changed, or its heartbeat still advanced 3 s after the group ended). DECISION RULE, per OS: an arm is eligible when it has three runs, every run is eligible, and (for G and GT) the OS controls passed. S must be eligible and the controls measurable, or the OS gets no verdict. No eligible sharded arm gives reject. Otherwise take the eligible sharded arm with the smaller median step_seconds (a tie goes to the arm without a tail) and adopt it only if its median is at most 3/5 of the S median and its slowest run at most 3/4 of the fastest S run, both compared as exact fractions of nanoseconds with no rounding before the comparison; otherwise reject, with no fall-through to the other arm. INCOMPLETE: a re-run (the compare job's own GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT, an input of compare.py, is not 1, or a run or control directory records a run_attempt other than 1), a cancelled or skipped job, a missing run directory, a job status cancelled (of an arm run or of the control run), an unrecorded run attempt (runtime.json missing or without run_attempt: a setup step failed before the run directory was prepared), a run whose test phase never started (its clock-start step's outcome, recorded from the steps context, is not success, or timing.json records no clock start), a missing control run or one whose parallel group never started (its foreground probe step did not succeed or left no probe), control steps that left no probe, log or exit status although the group started, when no other control evidence failed (a runner fault inside the control group), a controls-check job that failed although the compare job's own check of the same control artifact passed, an inventory job that failed without a report.json that records a gate finding (the gate never reported, or its own child interpreter was stopped from outside by SIGKILL, SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, which report.json lists under execution_problems with parity null), or an inventory job that succeeded although a file of its artifact (inventory.txt, module_ids.json, report.json or a shard list) is absent from the compare job's download (a partly downloaded artifact set, a runner fault) makes the OS incomplete, which is recorded as such and is never a rule outcome. NO VERDICT: an inventory gate that failed on a finding (report.json ok false with at least one problem), an inventory artifact that is present but unusable, an ineligible S or unmeasurable controls. ORDER: re-runs first; then a failed or unreported inventory gate (a finding gives no verdict, anything else incomplete); then the other incomplete conditions; then an unusable inventory artifact, an ineligible S or unmeasurable controls (no verdict); then no eligible sharded arm (reject) and the speed rule. A shard step that started but never reached its command or never wrote its exit status makes its run ineligible, even when a runner fault caused it; when the rule rejects or adopts while passing over a sharded arm that was ineligible only for that reason, result.json flags the arm and the outcome record must address the flag. ARTIFACTS: the compare job downloads the arm artifacts without merging, and a run directory counts only from the artifact arm-<run name>, which must hold nothing else (else that run is ineligible); any other entry is ignored and listed in result.json. result.json and summary.md list every preregistered OS; each workflow measures its own, and the other is listed as not measured, with the reason no run directory. The ubuntu-24.04 verdict decides a Linux adoption pull request and the macos-15 verdict a macOS one, independently. DECIDING RUN: A run decides an OS when its result.json, or, only if that file's upload failed, the outcome line compare.py printed, gives adopt, reject or no verdict for that OS; a run in which neither exists is incomplete. A result.json lists the OS that its run did not measure as not measured, which decides nothing. Per OS, the deciding run is the first run of that OS's own trial workflow that decides it. Until an OS's trial ends, a repeat is allowed for it only by closing and reopening the draft pull request when no run of either trial workflow is in progress. Once an OS's trial has ended, at its deciding run or without a verdict, nothing changes it: its later runs are reported only, and cancelling or reopening during such a run is not a deviation for that OS. compare.py writes summary.md and checkout-status.json first and result.json last, through a temporary file and a rename, and prints its outcome lines after that, so a failure before the rename leaves no result.json. PROTOCOL: Any coordinator action other than the close-and-reopen repeat that changes the head, or that makes a run incomplete after its first serial, shards or controls job started, is a protocol deviation that ends the trial of each OS it affects without a verdict: pushing a commit, or cancelling that run by hand, reopening during it or deleting its artifacts or the run itself. No run starts while the pull request conflicts with main, because GitHub runs no pull_request workflow on a pull request with a merge conflict: the trial of an OS that then still needs a run ends without a verdict (not measured), and no push may resolve the conflict. A run cancelled before its first serial, shards or controls job started is incomplete, not a deviation. compare.py does not see a deviation; the outcome record names it. Concurrency cancel-in-progress is true, so a reopen during a run cancels that run instead of queueing an unattended second run; because one reopen starts both workflows, a repeat for one OS waits until the other OS's run has ended, or has been cancelled once that OS's trial ended. RE-RUNS: no job is ever re-run, the compare job included, and any re-run makes the OS incomplete; every upload sets overwrite false; every run and attempt is reported, with the reason for each repeat and, for every cancelled run, what cancelled it. The record of a run is result.json, the exit files and the job results, never the rendered step summary or log annotations.
predeclared_metrics.usage_rule: No usage claim. The hosted runs execute deterministic commands and no model; their usage fields are observed zeros for deterministic execution, never a savings claim. The model usage of the sessions that planned and built this trial is not recorded here and stays unknown; it is neither estimated nor counted as zero.

runtime_and_platform.isolation: A draft pull request that is never merged. The workflows trigger only on that pull request's opened and reopened events with a paths filter on their own files, run with contents: read, persist-credentials false and no secrets, and change no other workflow, required check or ruleset. Each job runs on a fresh hosted VM. Run directories, the control suite and the inventory live under RUNNER_TEMP, outside the checkout, and the checkout must be clean after every run. Artifacts are kept 30 days.

commands: One parallel group of N shard steps (N = 4 on ubuntu-24.04, 3 on macos-15), each python3 -m unittest -v <the test files of its list>, then for G4T and G3T the serial tail python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_secret_path_guard

Controls: the shard step body in one parallel group on test_ctl_pass, test_ctl_fail, test_ctl_crash and test_ctl_hang (step ids control-0 to control-3, timeout-minutes 5, 5, 5 and 1), then python3 blueprints/convergence-practice/suite-shards-trial-20261003/record.py finish <results>/<os>-controls --os <os> --arm controls --repeat 1 --heartbeat <control suite>/test_ctl_hang.heartbeat (with STEPS_JSON, the job's toJSON(steps)), then in the controls-check job python3 blueprints/convergence-practice/suite-shards-trial-20261003/compare.py controls --artifact <results>/controls --os <os> --job-result <needs.controls.result> --expected-sha <head>

Oracle: python3 -m unittest discover -s blueprints/convergence-practice/suite-shards-trial-20261003 -p test_*.py -v; then python3 blueprints/convergence-practice/suite-shards-trial-20261003/compare.py verdict --results <results, one directory per downloaded artifact> --inventory <inventory> --expected-sha <head> --run-attempt <the compare job's GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT> --os <os> --needs needs.json --out result.json --summary-md summary.md --checkout-status checkout-status.json
limitations: Planned only. No GitHub-hosted run exists for this record. The evidence so far is local integration evidence (the coordinator's whole-suite preflight, this unit's inventory gate at the base, the oracle's dry run on the preflight's real logs), synthetic fixtures (real local runs of a fixture suite and of the controls, on which the oracle's own 112 tests run), a local probe of zizmor on planted constructs and source review (the GitHub documentation, GitHub's workflow schema and the runner source, CPython and the alternatives at their pins). None of it is upstream acceptance or a hosted measurement.

The preflight ran on another machine (48 cores, against 4 vCPUs and 3 cores on the hosted runners), another CPython patch release (3.13.16, against the Linux runner's 3.12) and an earlier base (d2777ee7, 233 test files, against 234 at the trial base). Its shard lists differ from the trial's in how the small files are partitioned, and the trial adds one file, so its equality evidence covers different process groupings than the hosted runs will use.

n = 3 runs per arm. Hosted wall-clock time varies with neighbours and image updates (the first trial's three serial Linux runs took 1,186 to 1,688 s on one image); three repeats bound this loosely. Job seconds from the jobs API are reported beside step_seconds and are not used by the rule.
Hosted macOS has never run this suite in shards, and the first trial never ran on macOS at all.

Unmeasured hosted behaviour, each with the first-run check that settles it (README.md, 'First-run checklist'): whether a hosted runner starts background steps with SIGINT or SIGQUIT ignored, and whether earlier GITHUB_ENV exports and actions/setup-python's PATH reach them (the probes; locally, ignored dispositions skipped a SIGQUIT subtest, which the record comparison would count as a mismatch); whether timeout-minutes stops a background step, which the runner source does, when, and whether its Python process outlives the step, which the runner source leaves possible because it signals only the step's shell (the hang control's step outcome and heartbeat, and the controls job's step spans from the jobs API); whether the steps context carries a background step's outcome after the group's implicit wait, which GitHub's workflow schema and the runner source imply (the controls' meta.json steps; if any of the four control steps' outcomes does not arrive while no recorded one is wrong and every other control expectation holds, the controls are unmeasurable and the OS gets no verdict, which decides it, since a repeat would meet the same platform; only a recorded wrong outcome or another failed control expectation fails the controls).

A runner fault after the clock step that stops a shard step before its command or its exit status (a background step whose shell never starts, a lost step) makes that run ineligible, not incomplete, as preregistered, so it can hand the decision to the other arm or give reject. result.json flags a sharded arm that the rule passed over while it was ineligible only so (verdicts.<os>.flags), and the outcome record must address every flag; the flag does not change the outcome. The same fault inside the control group (a control step that left no probe, log or exit status after the foreground step succeeded) makes the OS incomplete instead, unless other recorded control evidence fails: a shard step is the candidate itself, which would meet the same fault in production, while the controls measure the platform for both arms, and a lost control step measured nothing.

zizmor 1.30.1 warns that its support for parallel steps is experimental (its docs/usage.md at v1.30.1, 'Parallel steps'). Measured on scratch copies: template-injection, unpinned-uses, artipacked and (under pull_request_target) github-env report a construct planted inside a parallel group exactly as outside it; other audits were not probed. The shard and control steps carry no expression, action, if or GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_PATH write inside a group, which test_compare.py checks in the trial's compare job and locally; the repository's required suite does not collect test_compare.py (blueprints/ is not a package), so an adoption pull request moves that plain-text check into tests/test_workflow_hardening.py, over every parallel group of every workflow. actionlint 1.17.0 parses the groups, their step ids and their scripts with shellcheck. The hosted validate job's online zizmor step (validate.yml line 70) has not run on the pushed head; its result is a first-run checklist item.

Verified by the coordinator on 2026-10-03 before the push: actions/download-artifact src/download-artifact.ts at 3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c, lines 185-198 (read with a GET request), sets the download path to the target directory itself when the download is a single artifact, merge-multiple is set or exactly one artifact matched, so the pattern download of the control artifact lands as results/controls/<os>-controls; a nested path would leave the control run absent, which compare.py counts as incomplete, never as a wrong attribution. git diff --name-only 9b0b8d6d 1809afba over .claude/agents, adoption/agents, examples/claude-native/agents and .codex is empty, and no later commit of the branch touches those paths: the branch changes no agent definition.

Re-runs are not permitted, so the first run cannot settle what a re-run would do: whether a re-run job's upload (overwrite false) collides with the first attempt's artifact of that name or creates a second one, and whether a job re-run also re-runs the jobs that need it (the re-run page of github/docs at a3e0414f does not say). compare.py makes the OS incomplete in each case; if a re-run happens anyway, the run's attempts and artifact listing (GET) settle which applied.

macOS slots: this pull request changes manifests/evidence.json, an adoption-bootstrap.yml path, and adoption-bootstrap.yml's pull_request trigger takes the default types, so the opening and every reopen also start bootstrap-macos, bootstrap-macos-brew and validate-macos: with this record's serial, sharded and control jobs, up to six macOS jobs against the plan's five slots, each time, the queueing hazard that kept the first trial's macOS jobs from starting. Queue time does not enter step_seconds; a stall that ends in cancellation makes the OS incomplete, unless the run was cancelled by hand after its first serial, shards or controls job started (a protocol deviation). The coordinator opens, and reopens, the pull request only when the macOS queue is not saturated and reads it before and after each.

step-security/harden-runner audits egress on macos-15 only if its agent starts; a previous hosted validate-macos run logged a non-fatal installation warning (evidence/artifacts/wsl-retrieval-retirement-20261003/ci-correction.md, line 7). The first run reads one macos-15 job's harden-runner log; if the agent did not start, the outcome record says macOS egress was unaudited. The jobs hold no secret and a read-only token.

Artifact attribution checks names and layout, not authorship: every arm job runs the pull request head, so a head that writes another run's directory makes only its own run ineligible, and a head that rewrites its own run directory is caught only by the oracle's other rules. The logs and the step summary carry text the pull request controls; the record is result.json, the exit files and the job results.

The macOS inventory is built on ubuntu-24.04 with the arms' Python line from the same actions/setup-python pin, so that a stalled macOS queue cannot hold it. A platform-dependent id would make every macOS S run ineligible (its executed ids must equal the inventory), which gives no verdict, not a wrong one.

The trial environment is not production's. Every arm adds -v, which Linux production lacks. The macOS arms install the two npm pins that validate-macos (a recorded gap of the runtime tripwires) does not, so those tests run in the trial and skip in production; the macOS arms also skip validate-macos's validators and bootstrap and recording smoke.

Skip reasons are not compared (the parser reads skipped '<reason>' as skipped), and side effects that leave outcomes unchanged are invisible to the oracle. Test files that share a shard share a process; files in different shards do not, so any coupling between files shows only through outcomes.

tests.test_secret_path_guard.K4GuardTests.test_k4_timing is timing-bound (30 to 60 s serially) and failed under class-level parallel load in the first trial; the T arms keep its module out of the parallel group, the G arms do not. A mismatch on it counts under the rule like any other; only the flaky-id rule excludes an id.
A file newer than the weights takes the mean weight: at the base, tests.test_catalog_freshness_runtime (5,450 ms assumed, 0.23 s locally), so its shard is predicted about 5 s heavier than it is.

Run directories and artifacts expire (artifacts after 30 days, run records under the repository's 90-day retention), so the observed record keeps sanitized durable receipts in the repository rather than run links alone. Hosted logs carry runner paths in tracebacks; scripts/validate.py rejects home paths, so receipts must be sanitized first.

The workflows, the generator, the weights, the inventory gate, the recorder, the parser, the oracle, its tests, the fixture tool, the fixture index, the controls and README.md are frozen here by hash; any later edit to one of them must refreeze this record in the same commit. The fixture logs are frozen through fixtures/index.json, which test_compare.py checks. The checker verifies declared consistency and artifact hashes, not truth or that this freeze preceded execution; the commit history and the hosted run timestamps show the order. No trial job checks the frozen sha256s at run time. Validate (validate.yml) runs on every push to the pull request while it does not conflict with main and re-hashes them (scripts/validate_convergence.py --all-recorded checks every path and sha256 entry of each record in convergence_records, this planned one included, whatever its status; scripts/validate.py checks every manifest row), so a push that edits a frozen file without refreezing fails it and one that refreezes passes it. Every run records the head it tested (meta.json checkout_sha, result.json inputs.expected_sha), which the outcome record compares with the first run's; a changed head is a protocol deviation.

decision_and_scope.scope: The draft pull request that holds this record and its two trial workflows, never merged: the preregistered comparison of sharded arms (GitHub parallel steps, one unittest process per shard) against the serial whole-suite command on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 and macos-15 runners at its head. Nothing is adopted under this planned record; validate and validate-macos keep their serial commands unless an observed record meets the rule for that OS and a separate adoption pull request lands through the required checks.

rollback: Close the draft pull request. It is never merged, so main, the required checks, the rulesets and both production workflows stay unchanged; its artifacts expire after 30 days. If an adoption pull request lands later, reverting it restores the serial command (python3 -m unittest in validate, python3 -m unittest -v in validate-macos).

Otherwise record reject, no verdict or incomplete as a failed or partial attempt and keep the serial command. To triage first, read the inventory job's report (its findings and execution problems), then the controls in result.json (each control step's own outcome, whether they are unmeasurable or lost a step, the probes' starts, the hang step's stop and its deadline) and each control shard's probe (background SIGINT and SIGQUIT dispositions, SUITE_SHARDS_ENV_PROBE, python version), then every flag and the first ineligible run's reasons in result.json.
